text: Bulgaria submitted the National Plan for Diversification of Natural Gas Supplies to the European Commission (07.05.2026 13:20)

Bulgaria has officially submitted to the European Commission its National Plan for Diversification of Natural Gas Supplies, prepared in accordance with the new European regulation on the gradual phase-out of imports of Russian gas, the Ministry of Energy announced. The document presents the country’s comprehensive strategy for ensuring secure, sustainable, and competitive supplies, based on alternative sources, new routes, and modernized infrastructure.

The plan places a strong emphasis on the development of the Vertical Gas Corridor, the expansion of intersystem connections, the increase of the capacity of the Chiren gas storage facility, and access to international LNG markets.

By preparing the plan, we demonstrated a proactive stance, contributing to the achievement of the common European goal of energy independence and resilience, the interim Minister of Energy, Traicho Traikov, emphasized on this occasion, as quoted in the statement. According to him, the document reinforces the country’s leading role in ensuring energy security for the economies and citizens of the Old Continent.

The European Commission was informed that the country is already implementing key measures, including infrastructure projects, optimization of system flexibility, and coordination mechanisms between institutions and operators. The plan emphasizes that the actions taken are fully aligned with the principles of solidarity and the free movement of gas within the EU.

With this strategic document, Bulgaria shows that it is acting in a timely, consistent manner and in full alignment with European objectives, turning diversification into a real, measurable, and sustainable policy, Minister Traikov also said. The country demonstrates that it has concrete projects, clear deadlines, and a stable vision for the future of the energy system.

The submission of the plan underscores Bulgaria’s role as a reliable partner in the regional energy architecture and an active participant in building modern, interconnected, and competitive infrastructure. The document sends a clear signal that the country is working consistently to reduce dependencies, increase supply security, and strengthen the resilience of the European energy market.

With the presentation of the National Plan, Bulgaria reaffirms its commitment to the common European goals and demonstrates that it is turning political priorities into concrete actions that have a real impact on the country and the region, the Ministry of Energy added.
